text: Shell reports $10.81 billion in quarterly adjusted earnings, up from $5.43 billion, with record indicative refining margins of $42 per barrel. Free cash flow rises to $16.3 billion, net debt falls to $39.7 billion, and the company announces a $5 billion share buyback program.

meta.note: Record refining margins reflect sector-wide conditions; announced buybacks are not completed distributions.

text: ECB President Christine Lagarde announces her departure for February 7, 2027, nine months before her term expires. The European Council's appointment process begins amid simultaneous senior leadership vacancies, national representation considerations, and elevated French sovereign bond spreads.

meta.note: Successor selection remains unresolved; monetary policy independence and political appointment authority are institutionally distinct.

text: Eli Lilly reports $24.4 billion in quarterly revenue, with Mounjaro sales up 65% and Zepbound up 49%. U.S. volume rises 41% while realized prices fall 7%. Lilly holds 63% of the U.S. obesity and diabetes drug market. New oral treatment Foundayo generates $184 million, below estimates.

meta.note: Market share covers obesity and diabetes drugs; Foundayo's performance differs from established injectable treatments.

text: U.S. GDP grows 3.4% annualized in Q3, with private domestic investment up 19.4% and consumer spending up 3.8%. September headline PCE inflation reaches 3.6% annually, while core PCE reaches 3.1%. Monthly consumer spending rises 0.5%, compared with 0.2% personal income growth.

meta.note: GDP figures are quarterly annualized rates; PCE inflation and income-spending figures use different measurement periods.

text: The ECB unanimously holds its deposit rate at 2.5% as euro area inflation reaches 3.8% and energy inflation rises to 18.8%. Average 10-year sovereign yields increase approximately 35 basis points. Underlying inflation and wages remain broadly stable, while the euro area economy continues expanding.

meta.note: December rate expectations reflect market pricing, not an announced policy commitment.

text: Alphabet shares decline 12% in morning trading while Microsoft remains largely unchanged. Alphabet reports negative quarterly free cash flow of $9.07 billion against Microsoft's positive $18.63 billion. Alphabet's search revenue grows 12% to $63.35 billion, below analyst expectations.

meta.note: Share-price movements are intraday; differing cash flow positions do not independently establish investment returns.

text: Intel reports $16.51 billion in quarterly revenue, up 21%, with data center and AI revenue rising 78% to $7.3 billion while client computing revenue falls 5% to $8.1 billion. Fourth-quarter guidance trails estimates, an Israeli fab remains disrupted, and shares decline 21% after hours.

meta.note: Fourth-quarter guidance is prospective; foundry production capacity remains distinct from confirmed external customer demand.

text: Starbucks reports $9.14 billion in quarterly revenue, down 4%, while net income rises to $677.2 million. U.S. same-store sales grow 7.7% against 0.9% internationally. Global transactions increase 1.8%. The China joint venture changes consolidated revenue recognition as the company adds 303 net new cafes.

meta.note: Reported revenue contraction includes the China accounting transition; comparable sales and consolidated revenue are distinct measures.
